title: A Narwhal-Inspired Sensing-to-Control Framework for Small Fixed-Wing Aircraft
relevance: ICRA 2026 research on an E-flite Slow Ultra Stick, an adjacent Ultra Stick airframe. A two-axis rig and six-axis load cell measure the instrumented model while two five-hole probes, seven right-wing pressure taps, four independently controlled surfaces, and an upstream gust generator are exercised. The paper reports force-estimation and closed-loop tracking results across 7, 9, 10, and 14 m/s conditions.
limitations: This is a wind-tunnel-mounted model, not a free-flight campaign or a published full-airframe coefficient table. Its headline 6D wrench RMSE combines N and N·m, so it is comparative rather than a physically homogeneous metric. No raw synchronized sensor/force logs or dataset link was exposed on the paper or authors’ project page. Results should not be transferred as Jensen Ugly Stik coefficients.

The authors’ project page identifies the work as ICRA 2026, and Crossref DOI metadata identifies it as a proceedings article in the 2026 IEEE ICRA proceedings (DOI 10.1109/ICRA57385.2026.11697429; published 2026-06). license: No reuse license stated in the downloaded PDF; retain as a local research reference and do not infer redistribution permission.
read_depth: Full 8-page arXiv v2 parsed; hardware, probe calibration, experiment stages, tabulated errors, and limitations reviewed. No raw data extraction.

relevance: A University of Minnesota thesis that develops stochastic electric-propeller thrust and aerodynamic models. Its indexed outline says the aerodynamic-model method is validated using a Mini Ultra-Stick; the abstract reports wind-tunnel validation of the thrust uncertainty model and an aerodynamic-coefficient uncertainty model based on wind-tunnel experiments.
limitations: The thesis is known from the University Digital Conservancy bitstream text indexed by search and from its citation in Lie’s 2014 UMN dissertation; the full thesis was not retrieved. title: Bio-inspired Distributed Strain and Airflow Sensing for Small Unmanned Air Vehicle Flight Control
relevance: The primary abstract reports two modified UAV platforms: one with 12 wing strain gauges and one with four chordwise pressure sensors. It covers wind-tunnel, indoor free-flight, and outdoor free-flight observations, controlled gusts and natural turbulence, and sensor-based roll or pitch control. This adds real-flight flow-sensing evidence around the Stick-class research-platform literature.
limitations: The accessible institutional abstract does not identify the aircraft models or publish geometry, inertias, aerodynamic derivatives, or raw telemetry. This is sensor/control evidence rather than a validated general flight-dynamics model. The full AAM could not be inspected, and its campaign relationship to the group’s 2019 pressure-sensing paper is not established.

title: Towards High Speed Aerial Tracking of Agile Targets
relevance: Primary flight-test system-identification study on a custom Kadet Senior UAV. It records pitot airspeed, alpha/beta vanes, IMU attitude/rates and acceleration, and four RC PWM references; the thesis reports an initial Output Error fit and an improved 23-parameter model after smoothing noisy MEMS rates. The acquisition system is described at about 75 Hz with synchronized sampling.
limitations: The thesis includes plots, not the underlying flight-log files. Control inputs are RC receiver references rather than measured servo/surface positions, and the author identifies wind, MEMS drift/noise, vane calibration and initial-parameter sensitivity as material errors. Aggressive nonlinear-controller trajectories are simulated; the airframe was flight-tested with linear control only and was judged structurally unsuitable for aggressive maneuvers. Exact loaded mass, motor and propeller configuration are not established in the identification section.
access: Public direct PDF from the University of Waterloo repository; downloaded and parsed in full (94 pages).
license: Copyright retained by author; no broader redistribution license inferred. Local research reference copy.
read_depth: Full 94-page thesis parsed; acquisition hardware, channels, timing, model fitting, flight results and limitations reviewed.

title: Experimental Validation of Total Energy Control System for UAVs
relevance: Public primary paper using actual Kadet Senior flight telemetry to assess TECS/EKF and compare flight responses with theoretical and hardware-in-the-loop models. It describes a 4.95 kg, 2.045 m span aircraft, 0.76 m² wing, 1.3 kW electric motor and 14x7 propeller. Reported TECS errors against flight references are 12.3% pitch, 5.5% airspeed and 11.1% relative altitude.
limitations: This validates control/estimation behavior, not a complete aerodynamic model. Pixhawk actuator commands are reported at 30 Hz and IMU at 25 Hz; the lower-rate telemetry link is 3.56 parameters/s. Inertias are calculated with XFLR5, while only angular-rate stability derivatives are described as flight-estimated. Raw logs are not released. The 2020 journal article with the same title appears to be a related/expanded publication on the Kadet platform and should not be counted as an independent airframe or flight-data campaign.
access: Official EUCASS PDF publicly accessible; downloaded and parsed in full (15 pages).
license: Conference PDF copyright terms not established; no broader redistribution rights inferred. Local research reference copy.
read_depth: Full 15-page paper parsed; configuration, sensor channels/rates, flight plan, model inputs, reported errors and limitations reviewed.

title: Implementación y validación de plataforma RPA en software de simulación X-Plane 11
relevance: Open institutional thesis comparing measured Kadet-40 flight responses with an X-Plane 11 model. The modified 5.09 kg electric aircraft used a Turnigy SK4250-650 motor, Hacker 70 A ESC, 13x8 propeller, 6S battery, Pixhawk 6C, BMI055 IMU, MS5611 barometer, MS4525DO pressure sensors, and potentiometer AOA/SSA vanes. Logged/analysed channels include airspeed, pitch/roll/yaw, barometric altitude, angular rate and RC output (RCOU). A wind-tunnel check of the pitot system reports 18 points and 1.4242 m/s RMSE; the vane AOA calibration reports 0.9881 degrees RMSE.
limitations: This is response-level simulator comparison, not an identified aerodynamic-coefficient model. The first campaign had only 5.5 s between inputs and overlapping responses; the later campaign selected elevator 3-2-1-1 and aileron/rudder doublets. The simulated combustion engine differs from the real electric propulsion, and response magnitudes differ materially. The thesis does not state flight-log sample rates or bundle raw log files; the comparison uses selected plots and replayed control inputs.
access: Public University of Concepción repository item and bitstream; downloaded and parsed in full (98 pages).
license: Thesis author permits partial or total reproduction for academic purposes; no commercial redistribution rights inferred.
read_depth: Full 98-page thesis parsed; airframe/hardware, sensor calibration, two flight campaigns, selected channels, simulation setup and comparison limitations reviewed.

title: Synthetic Estimation of Angle of Attack and Sideslip for Flight Testing of an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
relevance: Primary Telemaster Senior flight study using MicroPilot LRC2 INS/GPS, magnetometer, pitot airspeed, ground-relative velocity and attitude to estimate alpha/beta with the wind-triangle method. It compares calm and turbulent-weather Telemaster flights and reports that turbulence makes the estimates less stable. The actual alpha/beta reference measurements came from a separate Vector-P aircraft carrying an ICASIM smart boom, because the Telemaster could not carry that payload.
limitations: No raw logs are released; results are plotted. The Telemaster itself had no measured alpha/beta ground truth, so the reference comparison is across airframes and does not establish Telemaster aerodynamic coefficients. The official ABCM PDF button resolved to a malformed endpoint with a missing file ID; no PDF was acquired. The full-text index on the author page was not treated as a locally acquired original.
access: Official ABCM record and abstract accessible. PDF download endpoint is broken (missing identifier); no local original retained.
license: Not verified; no local reference copy acquired.
read_depth: Official metadata/abstract and author-page indexed text reviewed; no PDF or raw flight logs obtained.

title: Thor flight-test report — Flights 34–35 (2012-03-30)
relevance: Primary report for two Thor sorties. Flight 34 includes manually piloted roll and yaw upsets, recovery attempts, and sustained post-stall points with timestamped maneuver windows.
limitations: The report says the Euler-angle data need post-processing, its angle-of-attack polarity was wrong, and the angle-of-attack estimate fails when sensed pressure is too low. The retained Flight 34 LOC3 report entries use 20% and 16% throttle; the generic LOC3 procedure starts with a power-off stall, but these entries are not zero-throttle logs.
